meta.title: Hadron-level convention factors of Sherpa and Herwig at their default tunes

conventions.a: our samples, as the training samples: initial-state radiation on, hadrons with c*tau > 10 mm stable (K0S, Lambda, Sigma+, Sigma-, Xi0, Xi-, Omega- and antiparticles stable), neutrinos excluded, beam photons removed (D4)
conventions.c: as a, but hadrons with lifetimes below 1 ns decayed (c*tau < 299.79 mm: K0S, Lambda, Sigma+, Sigma-, Xi0, Xi-, Omega- and antiparticles; no other species changes status); neutrinos excluded, ISR on, beam photons removed. This is DELPHI's stable-particle definition (proper lifetime above 1 ns stable); OPAL (3e-10 s) and L3 (3.3e-10 s) are equivalent in practice, since no hadron lies between 0.3 and 1 ns
conventions.nu: as a, but neutrinos included in every observable
conventions.cnu: c and nu together: hadrons with lifetimes below 1 ns decayed and neutrinos included
conventions.b: as a, but initial-state radiation off (no beam photons exist); 10 mm stable, neutrinos excluded
conventions.beam_photons: status-1 photons with pT <= 1e-9 E (Sherpa writes them with px = py = 0, Herwig with |px| ~ 1e-19 GeV); the nearest other photon has pT/E >= 1e-5

meta.ratio: every entry is a plain ratio X/a (not X/a - 1) of the same observable in convention X and in convention a, each generator at its default tune; multiply a convention-a prediction by it

observables.distributions: fractions of all events per bin (D3), no renormalization over a range of bins; a bin ratio is the ratio of these fractions. Bins: delphi_y02 = DELPHI d11-x01-y02 (the all-particle thrust, D5), aleph_d54 = ALEPH d54-x01-y01 (91.2 GeV, converted from T to tau = 1-T); lo and hi are in tau
observables.one_minus_thrust: mean of tau = 1-T over all events (exact thrust axis, compute_hemisphere_shapes of gen/compute_efps.py)
observables.B_total: mean total jet broadening over all events
observables.rho_heavy: mean heavy hemisphere mass rho_H over all events
observables.P_win: fraction of all events with 0.05 <= tau < 1/3
observables.tau_win: mean of tau over the events with 0.05 <= tau < 1/3 (directlib tau_win; equal to the moment tau)
observables.nch: mean charged multiplicity over all events, the pipeline rule: charge != 0 (extract_particles_full_flavor.charge) among the 100 most energetic non-neutrino status-1 particles; in c the decay products count; neutrinos carry no charge, so nu/a = 1 exactly
observables.nbaryon: mean number of status-1 (anti)baryons (1000 <= |pid| < 1e6) per event, as the pipeline nbaryon; c/a = nu/a = cnu/a = 1 exactly (each decayed hyperon leaves one baryon, K0S none, neutrinos are not baryons); b/a from the per-chunk tallies
observables.window_moments: the 14 keys of thrust_targets_nlo_point.npz: means of f(tau) over the events with 0.05 <= tau < 1/3 (conditional on the window, like the calculation's targets; f = log tau, tau, tau log tau, ... with tau clipped at 1e-6 as in directlib.funs). The ratio of a moment over all events, <f 1_win>, is this ratio times the P_win ratio

estimators.c_over_a: same events: the c sample against the same events with the decays of K0S, Lambda, Sigma, Xi and Omega undone (conv_process.py col columns, convention a exactly)
estimators.cnu_over_a: same events: the c sample with neutrinos against its col columns (a without neutrinos)
estimators.nu_over_a: same events: the a sample with and without neutrinos, pooled with the c sample's colnu and col columns (convention a rebuilt, with and without neutrinos)
estimators.b_over_a: independent samples: the b sample pooled with the d sample's col columns, against the a sample pooled with the c sample's col columns
estimators.errors: statistical, from per-event influence functions (delta method): same-event ratios keep the correlation; independent ratios add the two relative variances. nbaryon b/a: chunk-to-chunk scatter of the per-chunk baryon totals (ratio estimator)
estimators.weights: unweighted, like the pipeline (Sherpa ISR-on weights change the means by at most 1.4e-4 relative, lmx_phaseA/conventions/results/summary.txt)

source.samples: lmx_phaseA/conventions (Phase A): Sherpa 3.0.4 (card of gen/gen_stageE.sh) and Herwig 7.3.0p1 (card of gen/gen_stageF.sh), e+e- -> hadrons at 91.2 GeV, each at the CENTRAL point of analysis/symmetry/envelope_test.sbatch (= the default tunes); variants: Sherpa b PDF_LIBRARY: None, c HADRON_DECAYS: {Max_Proper_Lifetime: 299.792458}; Herwig b e+/e- PDF NoPDF, c DecayHandler:MaxLifeTime 299.792458*mm; d = b and c. Per-event tables of conv_process.py; the HepMC records were deleted after reduction
source.data_dir: /mnt/beegfs/bassi/reweighting/lmx_phaseA/conventions/data (read here from an md5-identical local copy)
source.data_manifest_note: md5 of the sorted lines "<md5>  <gen>_<conv>/<file>" of all chunk files

targets.note: only keys, window, central and sigma_pert are read

application.note: decision D8: per-generator, per-bin factors, measured at the default tunes, applied to each generator's prediction after imposing the calculation and before mixing with (1-xi, xi); the uncorrected predictions are kept as well
application.DELPHI: c_over_a (hadrons with lifetimes below 1 ns decayed)
application.L3_nch: no factor (L3 18.63 is without K0S and Lambda decay products, our convention)

calc_uncertainty.note: the calculation's own uncertainty of each window moment: sigma_pert from thrust_targets_nlo_point.npz, and with the 0.2% floor the tilt adds (directlib)
